topic: Honest high-dimensional inference for the ATE with unrestricted discrete confounders. Observe n iid (X,A,Y), X in [d], binary A, real Y, consistency, conditional exchangeability, fixed epsilon overlap, known M>=1, cellwise mean envelope M, and conditional fourth central moments at most M^4. For d<=c_epsilon n log(en), define W* as the minimax worst expected length over uniformly (1-alpha)-honest intervals. Prove W* is of order M min{1,n^(-1/2)+d/[n log(en)]}. Construct one explicit polynomial-time robust heavy/light interval whose rare-cell four-cell Chebyshev factorial-moment statistic has a fully data-computable directly calibrated tail radius; Markov/Chebyshev conversion of the banked MSE result, union bounds, and generic median-of-means wrappers do not count. On triangular arrays with d=o(sqrt(n)), cell masses at least c_0/d, fixed overlap, and efficient variance in [v_0 M^2,v_1 M^2], prove endpointwise o_P(n^(-1/2)) equivalence to the cross-fitted saturated-cell one-step Gaussian interval and ratio-consistent influence-function variance, while retaining honesty without Gaussianity at the rare-cell transition. Prove a direct same-class confidence-length testing converse for the full width frontier. Use Zeng et al.'s n=9915,d=8196 401(k) application as the consumer. Tail calibration, robust blocks, polynomial constants, critical-value computation, and testing priors are solve outputs.

open_problems.open_problem: For the unrestricted d-category confounding model with fixed overlap and fourth-moment-bounded real outcomes, what is the minimax worst expected length of uniformly honest ATE intervals, and can a polynomial-time heavy/light Chebyshev-factorial interval attain M min{1,n^(-1/2)+d/[n log(en)]} with a directly data-computable rare-cell tail radius?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves the large-alphabet ATE MSE lower scale, leaves polynomial-approximation estimators to future work, and warns that its n=9915,d=8196 401(k) bootstrap and normal intervals may not attain nominal coverage.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Yanjun Han, Edward H. Kennedy

source_refs.claim: Low gives a testing inequality for expected confidence-interval length under uniform coverage, establishing that honest length is a different decision problem from point-estimation MSE.
source_refs.author: Mark G. Low

source_refs.claim: Best-polynomial approximation with unbiased factorial moments closes logarithmic sample-complexity gaps for large-alphabet functionals, but supplies MSE guarantees rather than honest causal intervals.
source_refs.author: Jiantao Jiao, Kartik Venkat, Yanjun Han, Tsachy Weissman

source_refs.excerpt: The missing upper kernel is a coupled four-cell Chebyshev reciprocal polynomial with unbiased factorial lifts
The proposal does not claim inference, adaptation to unknown M or sigma, sharp constants
The converse is supplied by the source-backed fixed-sample control-zero lower-bound leaf

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web anchor leaves a logarithmic gap between standard ATE estimators and its moment-matching lower bound, while the banked proposal closes the point-MSE gap with a selected four-cell factorial polynomial but explicitly does not address inference. The rare-cell terms couple random occupancies, treatment-arm counts, and unbounded outcome marks; the banked covariance calculation is not an observable tail bound, and bounded-kernel empirical Bernstein results do not directly cover this random high-degree marked statistic under only fourth moments. On the converse side, the control-zero priors prove squared-error risk only: they must be rebuilt as a same-class test between separated ATE sets so uniform coverage directly forces interval length throughout the root-n, rare-cell, and saturated regimes.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample theorem giving a total polynomial-time heavy/light interval, an explicit data-only critical radius with uniform coverage, worst expected length at most C_epsilon M min{1,n^(-1/2)+d/[n log(en)]}, and a fixed-sample two-prior testing lower bound of the same order.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative connects unrestricted categorical adjustment, unseen-cell information loss, the logarithmic estimator gap, and visibly unreliable 401(k) intervals.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Unrestricted discrete adjustment defeats smoothness and sparsity -> unseen cells impose a d/[n log n] information barrier -> existing bootstrap and Gaussian intervals are unreliable when n is comparable to d -> sharp honest confidence length and a constructive interval are needed

method_exemplars.technique: Split light and heavy coordinates, approximate the nonsmooth functional by a degree-log n polynomial, lift monomials by factorial moments, and prove matching aggregate bias and variance bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The banked ATE estimator has the same effective-sample-enlargement architecture, but its polynomial is multivariate, treatment-arm-coupled, and outcome-marked.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct jointly robust location and scale M-estimators under bounded variance and kurtosis and prove confidence-dependent nonasymptotic deviations by PAC-Bayes exponential inequalities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a fourth-moment calibration primitive for outcome marks and observable scale; the new proof must integrate it into the factorial statistic rather than wrap the completed estimator.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert testing affinity and ordered moduli into expected-length lower bounds for uniformly covering intervals and construct intervals within constants of those bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested converse is about minimax expected length, so its moment-matched ATE priors must be used through coverage-to-testing logic of this kind, not through an MSE reduction.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one globally honest bounded-fourth-moment ATE interval also be endpointwise o_P(n^(-1/2))-equivalent to the cross-fitted saturated-cell one-step Gaussian interval, with ratio-consistent influence-function variance, on balanced triangular arrays with d=o(sqrt(n)) and nondegenerate efficient variance?

source_refs.claim: The paper records plug-in asymptotic normality when d=o(sqrt(n)), but does not prove uniform honesty, variance-ratio consistency, or endpoint equivalence for a procedure that also covers the rare-cell regime.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Yanjun Han, Edward H. Kennedy

source_refs.claim: DML proves asymptotically normal and efficient ATE inference from cross-fitted orthogonal scores under nuisance-rate conditions, not under an unrestricted growing categorical law with empty cells.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, Mert Demirer, Esther Duflo, Christian Hansen, Whitney Newey, James Robins

source_refs.claim: The paper proves self-normalized moderate deviations for Studentized nonlinear statistics, including U-statistics, under finite-moment conditions.
source_refs.author: Qi-Man Shao, Wen-Xin Zhou

source_refs.excerpt: Parametric risk holds through d=O(sqrt(n) log n)
The proof program does not address deteriorating overlap, latent effect groups, inference

open_problems.why_unsolved: Parametric-order MSE does not identify the efficient linear term. The random heavy/light decision, reciprocal-polynomial bias, and degenerate factorial components must all be o_P(n^(-1/2)) while the empirical saturated-cell influence-function variance remains relatively accurate as d grows. Standard DML assumes nuisance-rate statements that fail literally in empty cells, and generic Studentized U-statistic theory does not cover a data-selected statistic whose order and degeneracy change at the occupancy transition. The first new proof step is therefore a Hájek-projection expansion of the selected robust estimator, replacing the banked global covariance bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform-to-local bridge theorem proving global finite-sample honesty and, on the stated triangular arrays, efficient asymptotic linearity, ratio-consistent influence-function variance, and endpointwise o_P(n^(-1/2)) equivalence of the robust and one-step Wald intervals.

writing_exemplar.why: It places the sparse high-dimensional failure regime and the d=o(sqrt(n)) Gaussian regime inside the identical ATE model.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Saturated adjustment has a classical efficient influence function -> increasing d creates empty-cell bias and invalid routine inference -> balanced d=o(sqrt n) arrays restore first-order normality -> one interval should be honest globally yet merge with efficient Gaussian inference locally

method_exemplars.technique: Use cross-fitting and Neyman-orthogonal scores to isolate an empirical efficient-influence-function term and prove asymptotic normality with plug-in variance consistency.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The comparator interval is the saturated-cell specialization of this one-step construction; the missing work is a growing-occupancy remainder bound compatible with global honesty.

method_exemplars.technique: Decompose an empirical higher-order influence-function estimator into its first-order efficient projection and nonlinear bias-correction remainder.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired equivalence likewise requires a nonlinear rare-cell correction to vanish relative to the same efficient first-order influence function.

method_exemplars.technique: Studentize nonlinear statistics and prove a Cramer-type moderate-deviation expansion through projection and randomized-concentration control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The factorial correction is U-statistic-like, so proving its transition-scale negligibility and valid studentization requires control beyond an iid-sum CLT.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the sharp minimax estimation and honest-confidence-length dependence on the approximate effect-homogeneity radius sigma=max_k|tau_k-ATE|, and can one interval adapt over nested sigma-classes without knowing sigma?

source_refs.claim: The paper gives an upper bound involving sigma^2+d/n^2+1/n and a matching lower bound only at exact homogeneity sigma=0, explicitly leaving sharp minimax dependence on sigma open.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Yanjun Han, Edward H. Kennedy

source_refs.claim: The ordered between-class modulus characterizes expected-length adaptation across nested parameter classes and when honest adaptation must fail.
source_refs.author: T. Tony Cai, Mark G. Low

source_refs.excerpt: Neither object follows from the frozen primitives or the two attempted architectures

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web paper and banked follow-up agree that exact homogeneity and unrestricted heterogeneity do not determine the shrinking-radius wedge. The banked lower channel is hypothesis-independent and reaches only the product scale sigma^2 u, whereas its mixed-arm factorial lift retains singleton-pair variance and reaches the larger minimum scale; neither construction decides the frontier. Honest adaptation adds a between-class obstacle because nearly homogeneous and unrestricted laws may be statistically indistinguishable. Resolution therefore needs either radius-coupled fuzzy hypotheses with exact fixed-sample normalization or a new nonlinear estimator that removes singleton-pair noise, followed by an ordered-modulus calculation for interval length.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A matching theorem for minimax MSE and minimax honest expected length as explicit functions of (n,d,sigma), plus either one data-driven interval attaining those lengths over a stated sigma range or a matching nonadaptivity lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It introduces sigma as the natural continuum between homogeneous and unrestricted effects and explicitly identifies the missing dependence.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exact homogeneity makes within-cell collisions informative -> unrestricted heterogeneity restores the unseen-cell barrier -> sigma interpolates between the endpoints -> determine the minimax and honest-adaptation frontier in the unresolved middle

method_exemplars.technique: Compute ordered moduli between nested classes, derive expected-length lower bounds from tests, and construct near-optimal adaptive confidence intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The sigma-indexed causal classes are nested, making their result the direct template for distinguishing attainable honest adaptation from impossibility.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt treated-control collision counts, occupancy inequalities, and endpoint fuzzy hypotheses while retaining the heterogeneity radius in every separation and distance calculation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its collision and unrestricted constructions supply the two mechanisms that the missing sigma-indexed theorem must interpolate.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the uniform minimax honest-confidence-length phase diagram when overlap varies triangularly, epsilon=epsilon_n approaching zero or one-half, including the transition between the ratio-polynomial hybrid and the centered near-randomization interval?

source_refs.excerpt: Prove a uniform triangular-array minimax theorem for epsilon_n in [epsilon_0, 1/2]
No uniform triangular-array lower phase or sharp overlap-varying constants are claimed.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked polynomial theorem fixes epsilon before choosing its approximation constants, sample-size cutoff, and pilot misclassification bounds, while the centered near-randomization estimator supplies only an upper envelope. Its lower transfer likewise fixes epsilon and does not show that the moment-matched alternatives remain separated as assignment approaches randomization or weak overlap. Moving from MSE to honest intervals compounds the gap: both the directly calibrated tail and the coverage-to-testing converse need sequence-uniform constants, and the weak-overlap endpoint may cease to be point identified without additional restrictions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A triangular-array theorem giving matching upper and lower honest expected-length bounds as an explicit function of (n,d,epsilon_n), with a single data-computable interval, sequence-uniform constants, and stated transitions to random assignment and weak-overlap or partial-identification regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its fixed-overlap discrete-ATE formulation is the baseline whose constants and inferential guarantees must be made uniform near the overlap boundaries.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fixed overlap yields a sparse-cell frontier -> observational sequences can approach weak overlap or randomization -> fixed-epsilon constants conceal both transitions -> establish a sequence-uniform honest-length phase diagram

method_exemplars.technique: Retain epsilon_n explicitly in the overlap-constrained moment-matching experiment, fixed-sample transfer, collision bounds, and heavy/light risk calculation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The identical discrete-ATE experiment already contains the sparse-cell mechanism; the new theorem must make every constant and separation uniform along epsilon_n.

literature_map:
Zeng-Balakrishnan-Han-Kennedy (2024, arXiv:2405.00118) is the exact anchor: unrestricted d-category adjustment, plug-in MSE d^2/n^2+1/n, and moment-matching lower scale d^2/[n^2 log^2 n]+1/n.
Its discussion leaves best-polynomial ATE estimation and closure of the logarithmic gap open.
Its 401(k) analysis has n=9915 and d=8196 and cautions that bootstrap and asymptotic-normal intervals may not have nominal coverage.
Its appendix records plug-in asymptotic normality for d=o(sqrt n), but does not join that CLT to a globally honest interval.
Jiao-Venkat-Han-Weissman (2015) and Wu-Yang (2016) establish heavy/light polynomial approximation and unbiased factorial-moment amplification for large-alphabet functionals.
Wu-Yang (2019, arXiv:1504.01227) gives an explicit Chebyshev linear estimator and moment-dual converse for unseen support.
Paninski (2003, DOI:10.1162/089976603321780272) documents severe uncertainty underestimation for undersampled discrete functionals.
Low (1997) and Cai-Low (2004, arXiv:math/0503662) make minimax expected confidence length a testing/modulus problem distinct from MSE.
Hahn (1998), Hirano-Imbens-Ridder (2003), and Chernozhukov et al. (2018) provide the efficient-influence-function and cross-fitted Gaussian benchmark for regular ATE inference.
Catoni (2012, arXiv:1009.2048) gives direct heavy-tail location and scale deviations under bounded kurtosis, but not for selected factorial-moment causal statistics.
Shao-Zhou (2016, arXiv:1405.1218) and Robins et al. (arXiv:1512.02280) provide nonlinear studentization and quadratic-U-statistic normality tools for the transition regime.
Balakrishnan-Wasserman (2019, arXiv:1706.10003) shows that high-dimensional multinomial testing needs rare-cell-adapted statistics and may have non-Gaussian null behavior.
Zeng et al. also leave sharp approximate-homogeneity dependence, latent grouping, and formal inference for collision-based WATE/ECC estimators unresolved.
Targeted searches found no paper combining unrestricted categorical ATE adjustment, fourth-moment robustness, direct rare-cell polynomial tail calibration, minimax honest expected length, and local efficient endpoint equivalence.
prior_proposal_map:
Focused mining covered the accepted stat_discrete_ate_minimax_loggap/polynomial_upper_match and stat_discrete_ate_heterogeneity_frontier/v1 runs, the two closest discrete-confounder ATE predecessors.
For each run, the README, discovery/proto_core.json, discovery/writeup.tex, and current review JSONs were inspected.
The log-gap run supplies the computable heavy/light four-cell Chebyshev-factorial estimator and fixed-sample control-zero lower transfer.
Its honest_scope and general reviewer preserve a concrete open triangular-array epsilon_n strengthening.
The heterogeneity run supplies the real-outcome signed one-mark construction and a conditional-moment covariance proof, while explicitly stating that inference was not addressed.
Its surviving oeq:shrinking-radius-frontier records a product-versus-minimum rate gap and the obstruction in both attempted proof routes.
Angle reviewers emphasized reproducible calibration, radius adaptation, and the overlap phase diagram.
No angle-rejected archive exists in either adjacent accepted entry; the current target has only state and pipeline scaffolding and no prior proposal core.
